enquiry: We follow a coloured by-product in a fermenter with a UV/Vis absorbance method and want to move the spectrometer out to the control room. A chalcogenide infrared fiber cable is left over from an old FTIR project, and we would like to use it as the link to the probe.

clarification_questions.question: What goes wrong today with the current measurement, and what decision should real-time data in the control room drive?
clarification_questions.why: Clarifies the operational need behind moving the spectrometer and whether a remote readout is the real requirement.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Assumed the goal is remote real-time monitoring of the by-product trend in the control room.

clarification_questions.question: What is the target by-product's concentration range, and is it at ppm or % level?
clarification_questions.why: Determines whether UV/Vis sensitivity suffices and which absorbance range and path length are needed.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Level unknown; lab screening establishes whether it is ppm or % level.

clarification_questions.question: How does the fermenter broth look optically: clear, turbid or opaque, and does the colour change over the fermentation?
clarification_questions.why: Decides the probe geometry (transmission, transflection or ATR) and whether biomass interferes with absorbance.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Broth is turbid and colour varies; lab screening on representative broth decides the probe geometry.

clarification_questions.question: What are the fermenter conditions (temperature, pressure, fouling) and what cleaning or sterilisation is applied to the probe?
clarification_questions.why: Determines probe materials, mounting and whether the fiber and probe tip survive the process.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Conditions and sterilisation unknown; probe material and mounting are to be confirmed with the process team.

clarification_questions.question: What is the distance from the fermenter probe point to the control room, and what is the condition and length of the leftover chalcogenide fiber?
clarification_questions.why: Chalcogenide fibers carry only the mid-IR range, not the UV/Vis range, and their usable length must be confirmed before any reuse.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Distance and fiber length unknown; the chalcogenide fiber is not assumed suitable for UV/Vis transmission until checked.

clarification_questions.question: What reference lab method is used for the by-product today, and what accuracy does it deliver?
clarification_questions.why: Provides the benchmark against which a UV/Vis or alternative in-line method is compared.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Reference method and accuracy unknown; comparison design uses the existing lab method once identified.

clarification_questions.question: What accuracy, response time and budget are required for the in-line measurement?
clarification_questions.why: Sets the acceptance criteria and whether a simple UV/Vis setup or a more complex system is justified.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Requirements unknown; start with the simplest single-method option and define criteria in the lab trial.

rule_hints: nominal_range_not_instrument_range: A nominal method range is not the usable range of a specific instrument, fiber or probe. [DOCX §3; DOCX §5]

fiber_limits_wavelength: The fiber determines which wavelengths reach the probe. Silica fibers transmit up to about 2.4 um and cannot carry mid-IR; mid-IR needs chalcogenide, polycrystalline or hollow-waveguide fibers. [S02 p.6; S04 p.1; DOCX §5]
remote_measurement_nir_silica: NIR works with standard glass optics and silica fibers, which suits remote online measurement; robust silica cables of 100-300 m exist. [S01 p.5; S02 p.7]
do_not_invent: Do not invent measured results, accuracy, detection limits, response times, fiber lengths, product codes or prices, client facts, or guarantees. [DOCX §3]
insufficient_information_is_valid: If the known facts cannot justify a method choice, say so, ask the deciding questions and propose the next step. [DOCX §3]
